Commentary.Commentary: We have our Super Fours - Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, India and Pakistan en route to the next round, while others will take planes to their home. Just one more game remaining in the Group Stages. It's India taking on Oman. Do join us on the 19th of this month at 2.30 pm GMT. You can join us earlier for the build up. Till then, cheers!

Charith Asalanka, the skipper of Sri Lanka says that he is really pleased with the performance. Adds that it was almost a perfect game for them, the pacers doing well early and it was just the last over that went wrong. Says that Nuwan Thushara has been really good with the new ball and he always gets a wicket and bowls 2-3 overs up front. Mentions that the catches were amazing, Kusal Perera and Dushmantha Chameera were outstanding taking those. Tells that they want to be the best fielding side in the country in this format and always try to put their all. Ends by saying that the fans have been brilliant and hopes that they continue to support in the same way in the next round.

Afghanistan captain Rashid Khan praised Mohammad Nabi's incredible performance, particularly in the last over of the innings. Nabi's awareness of the spinner's upcoming over allowed him to play strategically, and his hitting of 5 sixes in that over was remarkable. Khan described the way they finished the innings as 'really special.' Khan noted that the pitch wasn't typical of Abu Dhabi's spinning tracks and that chasing a target of 170-180 would require good cricketing shots. He reflected on their previous game, where they missed a chance to chase down a modest total, highlighting the unpredictable nature of T20 cricket. Looking ahead, Khan emphasized the need for his team to learn from their mistakes and move forward. Despite extensive preparation for ICC events over the past three years, Afghanistan's performance in this competition fell short of expectations. Khan vowed to analyze their shortcomings and return stronger in the future.

Kusal Mendis wins the PLAYER OF THE MATCH AWARD for his match-winning innings. He says that he is happy with his knock and the result. Also praises Kusal Perera and Kamindu Mendis for the way they batted. Mentions that the Afghan spinners are faster than the others, so he tried to play behind the wicket more. Says that now they have to play three good teams in the Super Four, but they have a balanced squad and is looking forward to the challenge
...Stay tuned for the Presentation...

Rashid Khan's bowling changes were a bit questionable as well. Azmatullah Omarzai bowled superbly inside the Powerplay but ended up bowling just two overs while their heavy-spin attack failed to stem the run flow. However, if truth be told, Afghanistan needed more runs as Mohammad Nabi's lone magical effort in the fag end of the innings helped Afghanistan end on a high, but not with enough runs on the board.

Afghanistan struggled to pick wickets. They managed two scalps inside the Powerplay but Kusal Mendis blossomed at the top with contributions from Kusal Perera, Charith Asalanka and Kamindu Mendis to keep the scoreboard ticking. Sri Lanka needed one big innings from their top three, and Mendis answered with a fine, fine innings of high quality. His innings was nicely paced with a lot of running and finding gaps as the pitch got tricky to bat under the lights.

Two overs that changed the course of the game. Afghanistan were 120/7 in 18 overs, dead and buried as their batting failed dearly but cometh the hour, cometh the man, Mr. President, Mohammad Nabi went berserk in the last two overs as Afghanistan scored 49 runs with Nabi scoring five sixes in the final over. Afghanistan had all the momentum and with the tail up, they were expected to flourish with the ball but not to be.

Sri Lanka cross the line and are into the Super Fours but it's their arch-rivals Bangladesh who are enjoying as well. Yes, with Sri Lanka, it's Bangladesh who qualify for the Super Fours. Afghanistan on the other hand, had things in their hand but apart from that, TWO OVERS in the first innings, it was an abysmal performance.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length and on off, Kamil Mishara uses his feet but only manages to bunt it off the upper half of the bat towards mid off for a single.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nicely done! Fazalhaq Farooqi sees the batter advance a bit, bangs this into the pitch, on middle, angling in. Kusal Mendis picks up the length early and plays the short-arm jab in front of square on the leg side for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Kusal Mendis, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FIVE WIDES! Free runs for Sri Lanka! Bangladeshi hearts will be beating fast with every run here. Fazalhaq Farooqi loses his line and hits the length hard, on middle and leg, this one shapes a long way to the leg side. Kusal Mendis fails to glance it away, and Rahmanullah Gurbaz also fails to stop it with a dive to his left as the ball rolls to the fine leg fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Kusal Mendis, 5 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Pitched up but just outside the tramline, Kusal Mendis lets it go. Wided.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on middle, nips back in, Kamil Mishara tries to play at it but gets an inside edge towards fine leg for a run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length and on middle, attacking the stumps, Kamil Mishara blocks it out well.

Commentary.Commentary: And again! Back of a length and outside off, shapes away, Kamil Mishara goes for the cut but misses. Rahmanullah Gurbaz dives to his left to collect it nicely. Just 2 runs and a big wicket from the over!

Commentary.Commentary: A massive appeal for caught behind, but turned down! Rahmanullah Gurbaz, the keeper, looks very interested, and Rashid Khan, after thinking for a while, goes for the review. Azmatullah Omarzai bangs this into the pitch around off, angling it away, Kamil Mishara slashes at it but looks like he misses. UltraEdge shows no spike, and Afghanistan lose a review early.

Commentary.Commentary: Touch fuller and on leg, Kusal Mendis clips it to mid-wicket for a run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on leg Kamil Mishara flicks it thorugh square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Azmatullah Omarzai to Kamil Mishara, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Kamil Mishara comes to the middle.

OUT! TAKEN! Are we seeing an action replay from the Afghan innings? They lost their first wicket in the 3rd over, and the same has happened here for the Lankans. Azmatullah Omarzai lands this back of a length and around leg, begging to be put away. Pathum Nissanka hooks it away, knowing that short fine is up in the circle but fails to keep it down and hits it from the bottom half of the bat straight at that fielder. Mujeeb Ur Rahman shows good reflexes and dives forward to take a fine catch as the ball was travelling really fast. A big wicket for Afghanistan as Nissanka walks back cheaply here. Sri Lanka are 22/1, chasing 170!
Commentary.Howout: c Mujeeb Ur Rahman b Azmatullah Omarzai
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Azmatullah Omarzai to Pathum Nissanka, OUT! c Mujeeb Ur Rahman b Azmatullah Omarzai.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! 13 runs off Mujeeb's first over! He bowls it short again and around middle, turns in,  Kusal Mendis goes down quickly and heaves it away to the vacant deep square leg fence for another boundary. Afghanistan were 26/0 at the same stage, but it started to derail from the third over.
